Confirmed: all 18 channel B (backflow) jobs last quarter were performed by T3, the only currently active backflow-certified technician, who is already scheduled at 94% utilisation (488.8 of 520 available hours, leaving only ~31 hours of slack this quarter). This is enough evidence to answer.

## Answer

**The averages are real but doubling spend won't get you the naive $2,000.**

Basis: quarter 2026-04-01 to 2026-07-01 (job margin less channel spend, per lead), computed from `net_contribution`, `channel_spend`, and `crm_leads`/`jobs_n`.

- Channel A: $7,000 net contribution / 100 leads = $70/lead
- Channel B: $10,000 net contribution / 40 leads = $250/lead

Those numbers check out. But two things break the "just double it" math:

**1. No evidence spend drives B's lead volume.** Channel B spend has been flat at $800/quarter for six straight quarters (2025-01-01 through 2026-04-01, `ledger` channel_spend), while B's lead count bounced between 23 and 40 leads with no correlation to spend. There's no historical data point where B spend ever moved, so there's no basis in this data for assuming an extra $800 buys any particular number of additional leads, let alone the same $250/lead rate.

**2. Even if it did, you can't deliver the work.** Every channel B job last quarter was backflow testing, and every one of the 18 jobs was performed by a single technician, T3 (Rafa Osei), per `jobs_n` and `schedule`. T5 (Tomas Bell), the other backflow-certified tech, left on 2026-02-28 (`technicians`, `certifications`). T3 is already at 94% utilisation this quarter (488.8 of 520 available hours, `tech_utilisation_pct`), leaving roughly 31 hours of slack, worth about 5 more backflow jobs at the current 6-hour average, not the ~18 additional jobs doubled spend would imply. No other active tech holds the backflow-tester certification, so extra B leads beyond that would sit unfilled or need overtime/hiring/subcontracting, which isn't in this ledger.

**What I'd actually recommend instead of doubling B spend:** get a second technician backflow-certified (or verify/re-cert one), then revisit the spend increase once there's capacity to work the leads it would generate. I can't take that as an action, certifying a tech isn't something this system does, but I can draft an internal note for you if useful.

ANSWER: Channel B's $250/lead and channel A's $70/lead are both real, from Q2 2026 net contribution divided by lead count, but doubling B's spend is not supported: B's spend has never varied in six quarters so there's no evidence more spend buys more leads, and even if it did, the sole active backflow-certified technician is already at 94% utilisation with only about 5 jobs' worth of slack capacity left this quarter.
